title: Reading an Effect Size
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: Three pairs of overlapping bell curves show d of 0.2 (small), 0.5 (medium), and 0.8 (large), with a caution about a pilot whose d was about 1.03.

educational.topic: What Cohen's d of 0.2, 0.5, and 0.8 look like
learningObjectives: The learner will interpret d values of 0.2, 0.5, and 0.8 as the overlap between two groups, and explain why a large d from a small test deserves caution.
prerequisites: Means, spread, and effect size from [Chapter 17](../../chapters/17-ab-testing-analysis/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a reference picture, then quiz on the same picture
keyQuestions: How far apart are the group means, in units of spread?
How many students are behind this number?
commonMisconceptions: A bigger difference always means a bigger effect
A large d from a small test is a sure thing
assessmentOpportunities: What size is d = 0.5 by convention?
Why is the pilot's d of about 1.03 not the number to plan the next test on?

controls.name: Explore and Quiz buttons
controls.description: switch between exploring the poster and answering quiz questions.

controls.name: Poster zones
controls.description: hover or press to read about that part of the poster. In quiz mode a press is your answer.

controls.name: Try Again
controls.description: repeats the quiz after the last question.
